title: e-footprint optimization evidence inventory

scope.statement: Complete for commits explicitly tagged [OPTIM] in reachable Git history as of 2026-09-16, supplemented by the January workbook and deck, changelogs, and preserved performance reports.
limitations: Commit subjects and release notes are evidence of intended mechanisms, not causal attribution to AI-assisted development.
Historical speed and memory factors often describe a component, model topology, or sequential story stage rather than the complete deployed user action.
Factors from overlapping groups must not be multiplied without a benchmark that isolates the interaction.
The January workbook's combined speed×memory number is a heuristic, not a carbon-footprint multiplier.

estimation_rules: Prefer repeated before/after benchmarks over release notes, commit claims, and retrospective estimates.
Keep CPU duration, peak/retained RAM, persisted bytes, network bytes, cache state, and completion probability as separate model parameters.
Apply a factor only to the share of a journey actually affected by that optimization.
Use low/central/high bounds when the evidence is historical or topology dependent.
Model cold, warm, recovered-session, and large-model paths separately.
Treat the no-optimization scenario as action-specific counterfactuals, not one universal multiplier.

optimization_groups.title: Selective recomputation and update graph
optimization_groups.mechanism: Track calculated dependencies, cache results and invalidate only affected branches after edits.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: January reconstruction assigns ~10× calculation speed; a later edit-path change reports ~30% less time (1.4×).
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: C — historical reconstruction plus commit claims
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: The 10× is a bundle estimate and overlaps later caching/pull work; do not multiply it by every recomputation-related commit.
source_refs: e-footprint/communications/articles/2026-09-ai-assisted-ecodesign-carbon-case/26-01-20 comment j’ai divisé par 1000 l’impact de mon application.pptx#slides-5-6

optimization_groups.title: NumPy-native time-series calculation
optimization_groups.mechanism: Replace pandas Series/DataFrame arithmetic with contiguous NumPy arrays.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: ~10× speed and ~2× dynamic-memory improvement in January material; changelog reports about 20× performance.
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: B/C — consistent direction, differing historical estimates
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Use 10× as central and 20× as high sensitivity until the pre-change revision is benchmarked on a representative model.
source_refs: e-footprint/communications/articles/2026-09-ai-assisted-ecodesign-carbon-case/26-01-20 comment j’ai divisé par 1000 l’impact de mon application.pptx#slides-7-8

optimization_groups.title: Float32 time-series precision
optimization_groups.mechanism: Store and compute hourly values as float32 rather than float64.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: ~1.1–1.2× compute improvement; 30–40% lower time-series memory (January heuristic: 1.7× dynamic memory).
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: B/C — implementation fact plus historical estimates
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Memory benefit is not a whole-process RSS factor; apply it only to the time-series share of memory.
source_refs: e-footprint/communications/articles/2026-09-ai-assisted-ecodesign-carbon-case/26-01-20 comment j’ai divisé par 1000 l’impact de mon application.pptx#slides-11-12

optimization_groups.title: Compressed values and lazy materialization
optimization_groups.mechanism: Keep repeated values compressed and defer expansion/deserialization until a calculation needs them.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: 2–3× faster serialization in a commit claim; up to 90% smaller serialized repeated values and ~4× dynamic-memory benefit in January material.
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: C — scoped commit claims and historical reconstruction
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: The 90% and 4× claims apply to compressible/dynamic data, not total files or process RSS; overlap with schema-v23 size gains.
source_refs: e-footprint/communications/articles/2026-09-ai-assisted-ecodesign-carbon-case/26-01-20 comment j’ai divisé par 1000 l’impact de mon application.pptx#slides-9-10

optimization_groups.title: JSON hydration and serialization fast paths
optimization_groups.mechanism: Reduce conversion work with faster parsers, direct serialization, smaller identifiers and deferred links.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Scoped claims include ~10× faster datetime/orjson components and ~15% smaller large JSON from compact identifiers; aggregate effect is unmeasured.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Component speedups should be weighted by their share of end-to-end import/save time.

optimization_groups.title: Explainability object and parent-retention memory
optimization_groups.mechanism: Release parent/explanation references earlier and use fixed object layouts.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Parent cleanup/related optimizations approximately halve memory in historical releases; slots reduce repeated load/destroy growth by 10–30%.
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: B/C — changelog and scoped benchmark claims
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Memory-growth results are allocator/workload specific and overlap attribution-source eviction.

optimization_groups.title: Occurrence convolution and vectorization
optimization_groups.mechanism: Replace nested occurrence loops with vectorized and FFT-based convolution.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: ~30× for the typical FFT step, ~500× for a six-year scoped convolution, and order-of-1000× for the original extreme path.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Do not apply to non-edge models or to the full request; benchmark share varies sharply with topology and horizon.

optimization_groups.title: Server, storage and network calculation fast paths
optimization_groups.mechanism: Avoid redundant loops/conversions in server, storage, network, data-exchange and autoscaling formulas.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Scoped claims: autoscaling 0.85→0.10 s (8.5×), data exchange ~30% faster (1.3×), storage ~10–15% faster.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Apply only when the modeled system contains the affected object type.

optimization_groups.title: Unit and time-axis overhead reductions
optimization_groups.mechanism: Cache unit lookups and remove repeated alignment, formatting and time-axis work.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Custom unit registry reported ~5% overall improvement; other fast paths are unquantified.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Broadly used but small; likely overlaps measurements attributed to larger calculation-engine changes.

optimization_groups.title: Legacy Sankey attribution caching
optimization_groups.mechanism: Cache repeated attributed-footprint properties during warm Sankey generation.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: ~100× warm Sankey claim for the affected cached-property path.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Superseded/overlapped by later attribution fold and pull-engine changes; not an end-to-end request factor.

optimization_groups.title: Scalar/vectorized attribution fold
optimization_groups.mechanism: Accumulate period totals as plain floats and remove hourly arrays from the Sankey fold.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Cold big-system fold 1.26→0.35 s (3.6×); real edge-heavy cold Sankey 436→332 ms (1.31×).
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Two fixtures show topology-dependent gains; use both as bounded calibration rather than one universal factor.

optimization_groups.title: Bounded attribution memory and streaming
optimization_groups.mechanism: Evict source-scoped intermediates, finalize formulas and avoid retaining entire attribution trees.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Implemented five-target benchmark: peak RSS 2,350.7→~642 MB (72.6% lower, 3.66×), latency 1.61→2.25 s (~40% slower).
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: This is a memory-for-latency trade-off. Model both resource dimensions; do not report it as an unconditional speed optimization.

optimization_groups.title: Pull engine and schema-v23 persistence
optimization_groups.mechanism: Compute on demand, invalidate affected descendants, and persist a minimal input/cached-output calculation graph.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Cached export 202.8→12.8 MB (15.8× smaller); current gates show 5.4× load-to-ready, 4.4–24.2× edit/read and 589.5→431.6 MB peak RSS.
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: A/B — measured release gates and current rerun
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: This is a later amplifier, not the origin of most savings. It overlaps recomputation, lazy loading and attribution-memory work.

optimization_groups.title: Interface request and model-build deduplication
optimization_groups.mechanism: Avoid fetching, hydrating, computing or saving the same model twice in one user action.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Several changes remove duplicated work; 'stop computing system twice on import' implies an affected-compute ceiling near 2×, but no end-to-end aggregate is measured.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Treat as request-count/work-elimination evidence, not a blanket 2× duration factor.

optimization_groups.title: Calculated-state cache and compact recovery persistence
optimization_groups.mechanism: Keep calculated models in Redis and retain compact recoverable inputs in PostgreSQL.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Redis hot-state reuse is described as a great improvement; schema-v23 cached-state benefits are quantified in G13, but this layer has no isolated factor.
optimization_groups.evidence_grade: C — architectural evidence, no isolated benchmark
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Counterfactual depends on cache-hit rate and session behavior; model cold and warm actions separately.

optimization_groups.title: Sources UI lazy loading and local row updates
optimization_groups.mechanism: Load the source table only when opened and patch edited rows without rebuilding the full table.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Eliminates unnecessary initial source-table work and full reloads; no reliable timing factor yet.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Best modeled initially as fewer requests/queries/rendered rows, then benchmark S4 directly.

optimization_groups.title: Comparison workspace and resident overlay
optimization_groups.mechanism: Hydrate each comparison slot once, build the active model once, and keep the workspace resident behind overlays.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Removes duplicated active-model construction (affected build work up to ~2×) and avoids reloads on return; no isolated end-to-end result.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Savings depend on navigation mix and cache warmth; benchmark as complete user journeys.

optimization_groups.title: Worker lifecycle and memory containment
optimization_groups.mechanism: Collect after requests, guard cgroup working set, recycle high-retention workers and avoid OOM failure.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Memory-guard observation overhead is 0–1.8% in calibrated completed runs; primary benefit is reliable completion, not lower per-request compute.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Model abort/retry/completion probability and replacement-worker cold starts separately from optimization savings.

optimization_groups.title: Front-end payload and dependency reductions
optimization_groups.mechanism: Use smaller chart bundles, self-hosted fonts and lighter client-side rendering paths.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Direction is supported by code changes; no consolidated byte or energy estimate is available.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Include only if browser/network energy enters the functional unit; separate from backend CPU/RAM.

optimization_groups.title: Import, startup and reflection caches
optimization_groups.mechanism: Cache signatures/defaults/lookups and reduce import-time or repeated reflection work.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: Mostly unquantified; individual commit messages indicate avoided repeated lookups and conversions.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: May matter under worker recycling and cold starts; benchmark instead of assigning an arbitrary factor.

optimization_groups.title: Miscellaneous micro-optimizations
optimization_groups.mechanism: Small loop, lookup, import and rendering improvements not defensibly isolated into a larger family.
optimization_groups.best_estimate_summary: January residual heuristic: ~1.5× speed and ~1.1× dynamic memory; later individual changes are generally unquantified.
optimization_groups.overlap_and_caveats: Use only as a bounded residual after named families; it is the highest-overlap category.

model_mapping.recommended_treatment: Benchmark representative mutations; use a bounded duration factor only on recalculated branches.
Use 10× central / 20× high for affected numerical work, weighted by its share of each action.
Apply 1.1–1.2× to numerical work and 30–40% to time-series memory only.
Parameterize compressible share; benchmark cold hydration separately from warm calculation.
Measure complete imports/saves; retain component claims only as diagnostics.
Use process/container memory measurements, not object-size sums.
Apply only to edge-heavy models and weight by profiled occurrence-calculation share.
Select factors by object mix; do not apply absent server/storage/network objects.
Treat as a small shared residual or benchmark directly.
Keep for historical chronology; exclude from current counterfactual if superseded by G11–G13.
Use 1.31× central and 3.6× high according to topology.
Model 3.5–3.8× memory benefit together with the measured latency penalty.
Use preserved legacy/current benchmark pairs by action; never multiply the headline gates together.
Reconstruct the eliminated duplicate operations and validate with request traces.
Model a cache-hit distribution; benchmark cold, warm-same-model and recovered-session cases.
Count avoided requests/rows and benchmark the S4 source-audit journey.
Benchmark the whole compare-and-return journey with resident and cold variants.
Treat as reliability/overhead, not a direct saving; include avoided failed work only in realistic retry scenarios.
Include only in an expanded client/network boundary and measure transfer sizes.
Benchmark fresh-worker imports and hydration; connect to worker-recycle frequency.
Use only as 1.0–1.5× / 1.0–1.1× residual sensitivity after explicit families.
